summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for expireAfterDays data age calculation; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [high] The `expireAfterDays` parameter specifies the number of days used in the date criteria for nominating documents for deletion, and MongoDB Cloud archives the data when the current date exceeds the date in this database parameter plus the number of days specified through the `expireAfterDays` parameter. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-clusters-onlineArchives-create.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/online_archive.md, https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/mongodbatlas/api-docs/onlinea

[low] The clock for data expiration starts the second the data is archived, and the data remains in the archive for the number of days indicated in the expiration rule based on metadata stored about when the data was archived. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/online-archival-to-delete-documents/222323

[low] Data expires from the cluster after the period of time set in the rule based on the date field in the time series collection, and then stays in the archive for the period specified in the expiration rule based on when it was written to the archive. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/online-archive-dates/226846

[low] To modify the number of days after which Atlas deletes archived data, you can enter or modify the number of days in the Deletion Age Limit section, specifying between 7 and 9125 days, or leave the field empty to disable the data expiration rule. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/manage-online-archive.md

[low] Atlas Online Archive data expiration is available as a Preview feature, and the 'Data Expiration' feature deletes data from the archive based on when the data was archived rather than a field inside the documents. (verified as of 2026-10-15) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/online-archival-to-delete-documents/222323

[medium] By default, Atlas does not delete archived data, but if a Data Retention Period is specified, Atlas deletes archived data after the number of days specified, which can be between 7 and 9125 days (25 years). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/configure-online-archive-standard.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/overview.md

[medium] The data expiration rule takes effect 24 hours after you set the Data Retention Period, and it takes 24 hours for changes to the number of days after which Atlas deletes archived data to take effect. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/configure-online-archive-standard.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/manage-online-archive.md

[low] Once data is deleted from the archive, there is no way to recover it, so you must define your rules carefully. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/enhancing-atlas-online-archive-data-expiration-scheduled-archiving

The maximum number of days for data expiration is stated as 9125 days in some sources and 9215 days in others. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/configure-online-archive-standard.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/overview.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/manage-online-archive.md, https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/enhancing-atlas-online-archive-data-expiration-scheduled-archiving, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/online_archive.md, https://www.pulumi.com/registry/pack
